svg.title: Kafka transactions: producer and coordinator steps
svg.desc: Read downward through producer steps P1, P2, and P3, then Transaction Coordinator steps C1, C2, and C3. The circle labels identify the two tracks independently of color. Initialize the producer once, begin each transaction locally, write Kafka output, send next input offsets, and request commit. The coordinator durably prepares the commit, distributes commit markers, and records completion after all marker acknowledgments. Each partition's read-committed visibility is constrained by its last stable offset and need not change simultaneously. The symbol a denotes pending transactional data, not an aborted record; c denotes a COMMIT marker.
svg.text: Kafka transactions: producer and coordinator steps
Kafka 4.3 • One transaction joins Kafka output and next input offsets

g.text: Producer
P1
initTransactions() runs once per producer: initialize, resolve prior attempts, and fence older
instances with the same transactional.id. beginTransaction() starts each transaction locally.
P2
Write transactional records to the Kafka Outbound Topic.
Call sendOffsetsToTransaction(next input offsets, consumer.groupMetadata()).
The Group Coordinator stores input progress; offsets are not one per output record.
P3
commitTransaction() flushes pending output and awaits successful sends,
then requests EndTxn(COMMIT) from the Transaction Coordinator.
Transaction Coordinator
C1
Replicate PREPARE_COMMIT in __transaction_state.
The commit decision is durable; the producer may receive success here.
C2
Send COMMIT markers to every participating output and offsets partition.
After replication, read_committed visibility remains limited by each partition's last stable offset.
Visibility need not change simultaneously across partitions.
C3
After all marker acknowledgments, replicate COMPLETE_COMMIT.
read_committed consumers do not wait directly for this final state.
Symbols used in the transaction diagrams
a
Pending transactional record (not an abort marker)
c
COMMIT marker
